e:
Right homonymous hemianopia = left optic tract lesion (retrochiasmal, contralateral)
Optic nerve = monocular loss; chiasma = bitemporal

Giant papillary conjunctivitis: large papillae on upper tarsal conjunctiva (contact lens/prosthesis)
Trachoma = follicles

Refractive surgery (LASIK/ICL) avoided <18 yrs (unstable refraction)
Spherical-equivalent specs better tolerated than cylindrical

Hammer–chisel injury = metallic (magnetic) IOFB → MRI contraindicated
X-ray/CT/B-scan are safe
Flexner–Wintersteiner rosettes + leukocoria in a child = retinoblastoma (RB1 gene)
Epiphora + ↑ corneal diameter in infant = buphthalmos (congenital glaucoma)

Yellow-white macular deposits = hard exudates of diabetic maculopathy
Soft exudates = cotton-wool spots
Dry, rough cornea (xerophthalmia) = vitamin A (retinoic acid) deficiency

Homocystinuria (cystathionine synthase deficiency): cysteine becomes essential
Ectopia lentis downward (Marfan: upward)
Lagophthalmos (incomplete lid closure) → exposure keratitis

Prostaglandin analogue (latanoprost) has no bronchospasm risk
β-blockers (timolol) contraindicated in asthma
Right homonymous hemianopia → left optic tract lesion (contralateral, retrochiasmal)

Painless ↓ vision c̅ grey-white pupillary opacity in elderly = senile cataract → phaco + IOL
Sugar control alone doesn't clear the lens
Limbal dermoid: congenital choristoma at limbus (often inferotemporal), seen in children
KF ring = Wilson disease → serum ceruloplasmin (↓es)

Fluorescein stains corneal epithelial defects
Seen under cobalt blue filter (green fluorescence)
Streaky, radiating light = astigmatism (different power in meridians → no single focus)
Congenital glaucoma: epiphora, photophobia, blepharospasm c̅ hazy enlarged cornea (Haab's striae)
Distance vision ↓es but near improves without glasses = index myopia (nuclear sclerosis ↑es refractive index)

Pseudoexfoliation: dandruff-like deposits on anterior lens capsule
Risk of glaucoma & zonular weakness
Intacs = intrastromal corneal ring segments → keratoconus (flatten the cone)
Painless slow-growing mass at lateral canthus since birth = dermoid cyst
Guttae + bullous keratopathy = Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy (endothelial failure → corneal oedema)

A: two dissimilar pictures (dog + cage) seen together = simultaneous macular perception (SMP)
B: two similar pictures blended into one = fusion
Stereopsis = 3rd grade (depth)

Orbital cellulitis = posterior to orbital septum; ethmoid sinusitis is the most common source
Painful ophthalmoplegia + proptosis; needs IV antibiotics

Marfan: tall, long limbs, ectopia lentis (upward) → FBN1 (fibrillin-1) mutation
COL5A = Ehlers–Danlos
